bib.title: S-LoRA: Serving Thousands of Concurrent LoRA Adapters

legacy_report:
SOURCE: S-LoRA: Serving Thousands of Concurrent LoRA Adapters. Sheng, Cao, Li, Hooper, Lee, Yang, Chou, Zhu, Zheng, Keutzer, Gonzalez, Stoica. MLSys 2024 (arXiv 2311.03285v3, 5 Jun 2024).
COVERAGE: 71,956 of 71,956 chars read (all pages, incl. appendices A and B, references skimmed). Clean extraction. Figures 5-12 data are plots, so only captions and text were read, not values.

VERDICT ON THE NOTE
- Llama-7B rank 8, A100 80GB, 5 -> 2000 adapters 8.05 -> 7.61 req/s: CONFIRMED (Table 3, setup S1).
- "vLLM OOM by 100": CONFIRMED (OOM at n=100 in S1, S2, S4). Paper text says vLLM-packed "can only serve fewer than 5 adapters". Note the vLLM baseline is not real LoRA serving: LoRA weights are merged into the base and m separate vLLM processes run under NVIDIA MPS.
- Merge-and-switch ablation: mostly CONFIRMED but needs tightening. Setup is S2 (Llama-7B, mixed ranks {64,32,16,8}) on A10G 24GB, R=2, cv=1, input and output lengths U[8,512], alpha 0.1 and 1, 1 to 5 adapters. The text says merge wins at one adapter, but "its performance declines with more than 2 adapters". So "beats only at one adapter" is a fair paraphrase, but the paper hedges at 2. The merge variant is also not PEFT: it keeps continuous batching and PagedAttention.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- S-LoRA is up to 4x vLLM-packed and up to 30x PEFT, with orders of magnitude more adapters.
  number: 4x, 30x
  setup: Llama-7B/13B, single A100 80GB, Table 3; vLLM-packed only runs at small n.
  quote: "Overall, S-LoRA achieves a throughput up to 4x higher than vLLM-packed when serving a small number of adapters, and up to 30x higher than PEFT, while supporting a significantly larger number of adapters."
  where: Sec 7.2, p.6
  Check against Table 3: S1 n=5 is 8.05/2.04 = 3.9x vs vLLM and 8.05/0.88 = 9.1x vs PEFT. S1 n=100 is 7.99/0.25 = 32x vs PEFT. S4 n=2 is 4.49 vs 3.83 vs 0.54, only 1.17x vs vLLM and 8.3x vs PEFT. So the 4x vs vLLM is a best case at n=5, and the 30x vs PEFT is at n=100 where PEFT runs for a shorter duration.
- Table 3 (single A100 80GB, req/s, S-LoRA / vLLM-packed / PEFT):
  S1 (7B, rank 8): n=5 8.05/2.04/0.88; n=100 7.99/OOM/0.25; n=1000 7.64/OOM/-; n=2000 7.61/OOM/-.
  S2 (7B, ranks 64,32,16,8): n=5 7.48/2.04/0.74; n=100 7.29/OOM/0.24; n=1000 6.69/OOM/-; n=2000 6.71/OOM/-.
  S4 (13B, ranks 64,32,16): n=2 4.49/3.83/0.54; n=100 4.28/OOM/0.13; n=1000 3.96/OOM/-.
  quote: "Remarkably, S-LoRA can serve 2,000 adapters simultaneously, maintaining minimal overhead for the added LoRA computation."
  where: Sec 7.2 / Table 3, p.5-6
  Caveat: the table caption says 100, 1000 and 2000 for S1, but Table 3 notes PEFT was not run for n>=1000 "as its throughput is already very low for a small n".
- Throughput flattens past about 100 adapters because the active set in a batch stays constant. Capacity is bounded by host main memory.
  quote: "once the number of adapters reaches a certain threshold (e.g., 100 in most experiments), the throughput of S-LoRA no longer decreases."
  where: Sec 7.2, p.6
- Unified Paging: KV cache and adapter weights share one pool, with page size = one hidden-dimension vector H. A KV tensor of length S takes S pages and a LoRA weight of rank R takes R pages. Ablations: S-LoRA-no-unify-mem and S-LoRA-bmm (no unified memory and no custom kernels, padded batched matmul) are both worse. The numbers are only in Fig 5 plots, and the text only says "noticeably higher throughput and lower latency".
  quote: "a KV cache tensor with a sequence length of S uses up S pages, while a LoRA weight tensor of rank R takes up R pages."
  where: Sec 5.1, p.4
- Tensor parallelism: LoRA communication is negligible against base-model communication. Base model: one all-reduce, 2(N-1)Bh/N. LoRA: 5(N-1)Br/N. Memory is optimal, with no replicated weight matrix. Going from 2 to 4 GPUs gives more than 2x throughput (superlinear, because the system is memory-bound).
  number: 5(N-1)Br/N vs 2(N-1)Bh/N; ">2x" from 2 to 4 GPUs
  setup: Llama-30B on 2 and 4 A100 40GB, n=10 and 100; Llama-70B on 2 and 4 A100 80GB, n=10 (Fig 8). The exact req/s are only in the plot.
  quote: "when transitioning from 2 GPUs to 4 GPUs, the serving throughput increases by more than 2 times."
  where: Sec 7.4, p.7; Sec 6.2, p.6
- Merge vs on-the-fly (see verdict above).
  quote: "with just one adapter, the merging approach outperforms the on-the-fly computation owing to a one-time merging cost. However, its performance declines with more than 2 adapters, primarily because of the time-consuming switch between adapters."
  where: Sec 7.5, p.7-8
- PEFT is slow even with one adapter. Cause: no KV cache and no continuous batching. In A10G S1, S-LoRA's max batch size is 30 and PEFT's is 6. PEFT throughput on S1 falls from 0.26 req/s at 1 adapter to 0.17 at 200 adapters, with attainment 0.0 throughout.
  quote: "in A10G S1, S-LoRA can accommodate a maximal batch size of 30, while PEFT can only accommodate a maximal batch size of 6."
  where: App A.1, Table 4, p.13
- Real workload: LMSYS Chatbot Arena trace, base models treated as adapters. The trace has about 26 adapters, average input 85 tokens and output 165 tokens, on S2 A10G. The result is the same pattern as synthetic workloads.
  quote: "the average input length is 85 tokens, the average output length is 165 tokens, and the number of adapters is around 26."
  where: Sec 7.3, p.6
- Adapter clustering (batching same-adapter requests first) has a small effect, and a small cluster count d is generally better. It can hurt latency and fairness. Early abort scheduling beats FCFS and LCFS on SLO attainment and user satisfaction as cv grows (Fig 10, Appendix B).
  quote: "the impact is not significant but observable, especially for larger α and cv. Generally, a small d can result in better performance."
  where: App A.2, p.13

OTHER METHOD FACTS
- Design: base model GEMM is batched, and xAB is computed per adapter with custom kernels (MBGMM for prefill in Triton, MBGMV for decode). The decode kernel was modified from Punica and was faster than the Triton version.
- Adapters live in host memory, the active ones are fetched to the GPU, and the next batch's adapters are predicted from the waiting queue and prefetched.
- Built on LightLLM. Iteration-level scheduling from Orca.
- Hardware: A10G 24GB, A100 40GB/80GB, host memory 64 to 670 GB. Metric: SLO attainment is the share of requests whose first token returns within 6 s.
- Workload: Gamma arrivals, power-law rates across adapters. Table 2 defaults: 7B @ A10G n=200, R=2; 7B @ A100-80G n=200, R=10; 13B @ A100-40G n=200, R=2; 13B @ A100-80G n=400, R=6; alpha=1, cv=1, lengths [8,512] for input and output, 5-minute traces.

LIMITS
- Adapters are applied to Q, K, V and O projections only. The paper says the feed-forward module is excluded ("excluding the feed-forward module").
- Footnote: Llama-70B uses non-official architecture parameters and no grouped-query attention.
- The vLLM baseline is a merged-weights multi-process workaround, not native LoRA. vLLM later added LoRA support, so the 4x claim has dated.
- Throughput numbers are synthetic traces, except the Arena trace which has only about 26 adapters. The "2000 adapters" runs use a power-law, so most adapters are cold.
- Table 3 mixes request rates and durations. PEFT was run for a shorter duration at n=100.
- Authors name future work: other adapter methods, better fused kernels, multiple CUDA streams to overlap base and LoRA computation.
- Adapter clustering trades latency and fairness. No quality (accuracy) evaluation; this is systems-only.
- Related-work mention that matters for the note's encoder section: PetS (Zhou 2022) did parameter-efficient serving for small encoder-only BERT models only. S-LoRA is decoder-only.

BUILDS ON: LoRA (Hu et al., 2021) including merge and add/subtract swapping; vLLM / PagedAttention (Kwon et al., 2023); Orca (Yu et al., 2022); Megatron-LM tensor parallelism (Shoeybi et al., 2019); Punica (Chen et al., 2023, concurrent, kernels reused); Triton (Tillet et al., 2019); LightLLM (ModelTC, 2023); PetS (Zhou et al., 2022).

CODE: none. Repo cited: https://github.com/S-LoRA/S-LoRA. Key formulas: h = xW' = x(W+AB) = xW + xAB (Eqs 1-2, p.2).

FIGURES (no image extraction run; captions from text)
- Fig 1 (p.3): separated batched base GEMM plus per-adapter custom-kernel LoRA add. Explains why batching works.
- Fig 3 (p.4): unified memory pool, KV and adapter pages interleaved, page = H elements.
- Fig 4 (p.6): TP partition strategy with fused all-gather and all-reduce.
- Fig 5 (p.6): throughput and latency vs adapter count for S-LoRA variants.
- Fig 9 (p.7): merge vs on-the-fly, S2 A10G, 1 to 5 adapters.

PROBLEMS: none blocking. Plots (Fig 5-12) did not extract numerically. Text has typos ("Unfied"). No embedded instructions found.
